body.subject: Codex judge verdict: item48-balances-chain-order-r1 = D
body.text: artifact=item48-balances-chain-order-r1 kind=code purpose=tri7 item 48 BALANCES-REPLAY-LOSER: chain-ordered balances replay in the node (code, 10 new tests, rehearsals on two archives) plus a guarded swap/verify/rollback deploy to DNS3, Pi and DNS2; decisions: commit+push to master, and deploy by the brief's section 7 worktree=/tmp/codex-judge-1hIQYX codex_grade=D judge=codex
reasons: Core chain-ordered replay is well-tested and archive rehearsals support the proposed fix.

The acceptance check mishandles a chain that advances during replay: it permits covered > chased, but then requires replay_target_height == covered. Production writes replay_target_height as the originally chased tip, so a valid advancing-chain build will be rejected. The Rust tests explicitly support mid-walk advancement, but the checker has no corresponding test.

The deploy harness runs `systemctl restart` under `set -e` without trapping failure. If the new binary fails to restart, the script exits immediately and leaves the new binary installed instead of performing the promised automatic rollback.
blocking_issues: Fix 5_balances_chain_ordered.py to compare replay_target_height with the start-line chased height, while requiring covered >= chased; add a self-test where covered exceeds chased.

Fix 4_tri7d_swap_verify_rollback.sh so every restart failure after swapping triggers rollback, including failures from the initial restart command; rehearse this branch with a binary/unit that fails to start.
polish_suggestions: Clarify that creating or overwriting `<bin>.prev-item` is a mutating pre-deployment action; the script currently labels all precondition processing as non-mutating.
Add an acceptance-check test for multiple start/progress sequences if retries can occur within one process.
